biased_pathways: JAK-STAT3 (via JAK1/2 phosphorylation of IL6ST Y* motifs -> STAT3 recruitment and phosphorylation; INSR kinase also transphosphorylates IL6ST tyrosines)
SHP2-MAPK (via PTPN11 recruitment to IL6ST pY759 -> GRB2-SOS -> RAS)
suppressed_pathways: PLCG1-Ca2+-NFAT (excluded adaptor - rigid helix geometry prevents PLCG1 SH2 domain from bridging INSR-IL6ST complex)
CBL-TC10 (excluded adaptor - CBL requires specific spatial orientation incompatible with rigid helix constraint)
SOCS3 negative feedback (excluded adaptor - INSR kinase does not efficiently phosphorylate the SOCS3 recruitment site on IL6ST)

predicted_gene_rationale.up: MAPK activation drives muscle structural/contractile genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN, MYL6, TPM2) and NOTCH3 (satellite cell self-renewal). PI3K-AKT upregulates CCND1 (cell cycle) and BCL2 (survival). STAT3 activation induces SOCS3 (feedback regulator). IGFBP7 is an INSR-responsive gene linked to insulin sensitivity in muscle. These are enriched in the P2_up (young-enriched) signature from the muscle aging atlas, consistent with the past wins pattern.
predicted_gene_rationale.down: Aged immediate-early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN) and stress/senescence markers (TXNIP, IL32, CDKN2A, IL6) are suppressed. MYF5 (myogenic commitment) and MYH9 (non-muscle myosin) are reduced as the cell shifts toward a more mature/youthful myogenic program. TTN (titin, a P1_up aged marker) is suppressed. NFKBIA is reduced as NF-kB signaling is attenuated. This mirrors the past wins pattern where aged IEGs and inflammatory markers go down.

mechanism_narrative: The INSR-IL6ST forced-proximity novokine (rigid_helix_20 linker, ~30 Å) brings an RTK (INSR, Tyr kinase) into close apposition with a cytokine receptor (IL6ST/gp130, JAK-associated). Under forced co-clustering, INSR's kinase domain transphosphorylates IL6ST's intracellular tyrosines, creating STAT3 and SHP2 docking sites not efficiently engaged by IL6ST alone. Simultaneously, IL6ST-associated JAK1/2 transphosphorylate INSR's juxtamembrane tyrosines, enhancing IRS1/2 and SHC1 recruitment beyond what INSR alone achieves. The rigid 20-helix linker (~30 Å) sterically excludes large adaptors like PLCG1 (which requires ~40+ Å spacing for productive docking) and CBL, biasing output toward PI3K-AKT-mTOR, RAS-MAPK-ERK, and JAK-STAT3 pathways while suppressing PLCγ-Ca²⁺ signaling. This biased signaling profile upregulates muscle structural/contractile genes and downregulates aged-muscle IEGs and inflammatory markers, consistent with a rejuvenating transcriptional shift.
